NAVIGATION EXERCISE 01
Checkpoint A

Grid C1

E 514 · N 1349 m

Control: Northern boulder of the pair, east side.

Follow the valley trail north to its west-facing bend in grid D1. Use the bend as your approach point, then head northwest to the two boulders. Identify the northern rock and check its east side for post A. Match the letter before registering.

Equipment: map and compass always in hand.

NAVIGATION EXERCISE 02
Checkpoint B

Grid H1

E 1296 · N 1319 m

Control: Burned-out car, rear (south) end.

Navigate to grid H1 and search for the rusty burned-out car. Its empty windows, buckled bonnet and scorched interior make it unlike anything else in the forest. Find post B behind the rear bumper, at the south end of the wreck. Match the letter before registering.

Equipment: map and compass always in hand.
North is map north. Coordinates start at the south-west corner of the chart.
The next destination is revealed at this post. No time limit.

NAVIGATION EXERCISE 03
Checkpoint C

Grid H4

E 1325 · N 763 m

Control: Raised water tank, east side beside the ladder.

Navigate south from B into grid H4, checking your compass rather than following the slope downhill. Look for the round rusty water tank raised on four legs. Identify the ladder on its east side, then find post C beside it. Match the letter before registering. Match the letter before registering.

Equipment: map and compass always in hand.

NAVIGATION EXERCISE 04
Checkpoint D

Grid H8

E 1296 · N 144 m

Control: Collapsed timber cabin, south-facing doorway.

Continue south into grid H8. The east trail can help with the long approach, but leave it when your grid reading matches the destination. Search for a ruined timber cabin with a broken roof and brick chimney. Walk around to its south-facing doorway to find post D. Match the letter before registering.

Equipment: map and compass always in hand.
North is map north. Coordinates start at the south-west corner of the chart.

NAVIGATION EXERCISE 05
Checkpoint E

Grid D8

E 648 · N 115 m

Control: Stone well, east side beneath the hanging bucket.

Travel west into grid D8. Use the valley trail as a broad reference, then make your final approach using the compass and coordinates. Look for the circular stone well with its timber frame and hanging bucket. Post E is on the east side beneath the bucket. Match the letter before registering.

Equipment: map and compass always in hand.
North is map north. Coordinates start at the south-west corner of the chart.

NAVIGATION EXERCISE 06
Checkpoint F

Grid A8

E 115 · N 144 m

Control: Crashed aircraft, tail (south) end.

Head west toward grid A8. The ridge trail helps you reach the western side of the forest; leave it for the final compass approach to the marked grid. Search for a small crashed aircraft with broad faded-yellow wings. Its nose points north. Find post F behind the tail at the south end. Match the letter before registering.

Equipment: map and compass always in hand.
North is map north. Coordinates start at the south-west corner of the chart.

NAVIGATION EXERCISE 07
Checkpoint G

Grid A4

E 115 · N 792 m

Control: Overturned wooden boat, west end.

Work north along the western side of the forest into grid A4. Check east/west drift regularly so the terrain does not pull you off your bearing. Look for an overturned wooden boat with faded blue sides and an exposed keel. Its long hull runs east to west. Find post G at the west end. Match the letter before registering.

Equipment: map and compass always in hand.
North is map north. Coordinates start at the south-west corner of the chart.

NAVIGATION EXERCISE 08
Checkpoint H

Grid D1

E 605 · N 1325 m

Control: Broken radio mast, south side beside the blue cabinet.

Navigate northeast into grid D1. Return to the valley trail for a reliable approach, then use the coordinates for the final leg. Search for a broken red-and-white radio mast with bent aerials and a blue equipment cabinet at its base. Find post H on the south side beside the cabinet to finish the circuit. Match the letter before registering.

Equipment: map and compass always in hand.
North is map north. Coordinates start at the south-west corner of the chart.
The next destination is revealed at this post. No time limit.
